text:
Jules: Heads up: ACME reporting their quantized endpoint (acme-q-1) is slower and has lower output fidelity since the overnight quant calibration push. They sent latency and a curl repro.
Priya: Can you paste the numbers and the exact request they used? Also which quant profile was applied?
Jules: Customer numbers: avg 420ms -> now ~820ms, p95 jumped ~1.8s. Repro they ran:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/instances/acme-q-1/generate -d '{"input":"Summarize the following policy...","max_tokens":256}'
```
Rolled out last night: model=v2-large, quant_profile=auto-calib-4bit via canary -> 100% @ 1779414000.
OpsBot: deploy.action: rollout complete acme-q-1 -> auto-calib-4bit @ 1779414000
Priya: I pulled the runtime profiler for the host serving acme-q-1. Key excerpts:
```
[2026-03-18T03:10:12Z] kernel_choice: matmul_4bit_mixed -> selected INT8_EMUL kernel
[2026-03-18T03:10:12Z] kvcache_hit_rate: 0.72 (prev 0.91)
[2026-03-18T03:10:12Z] batch_size_distribution: 1:71%, 2:19%, >4:10%
compute_time_per_token_ms: 0.95 (fp16 baseline ~0.48)
```
Priya: Diagnosis: calibration changed some weight stats so our selector picked an INT8-emulation path which is slower for tiny batches; also KV-cache hit rate dropped which increases work per request.
Mateo: Reproduced in staging with same profile and short prompts. For batch=1 the INT8-emul path does extra dequant+reshape passes that add ~0.5ms/token overhead. Profile trace:
```
kv_lookup: 0.27ms
dequantize_loop: 0.62ms  <-- new after calib
matmul_int8_emul: 0.88ms
postprocess: 0.18ms
```
Mateo: That extra dequantize step dominates for ACME's prompt lengths. Also saw tokenization/prefix differences that explain KV hits falling.
Alex: Proposed immediate mitigation: hotfix by pinning this instance to the FP16 variant until we fix selector heuristics. Low risk.
Priya: We have a runtime flag force_model_variant. I can set acme-q-1.force_model_variant=fp16 as a one-off. Plan: pin now, validate metrics, then run AB tests to adjust selector for small-batch workloads.
Jules: I'll notify ACME, but will wait until you've applied the pin so we don't flip them twice. Draft customer note: "Hi ACME, we identified a regression introduced by last night's quant calibration that caused our runtime to pick an INT8-emulation kernel and changed KV-cache behavior, leading to increased latency and some output drift. We're rolling your endpoint back to FP16 now and will follow up with a permanent fix within 48 hours. Apologies for the disruption. —Jules, Customer Success"
Priya: Applying pin now (ETA ~5min).
OpsBot: config.update: acme-q-1.force_model_variant=fp16 @ 1779428800
Priya: Pin applied @ 1779428800. Immediate metric snapshot shows instance p95 dropping from ~1.8s -> ~0.5s.
Jules: Sent rollback comms to ACME @ 1779428900; they acknowledged and confirmed latency looks much better.
Mateo: Action items: open an RFC to change kernel selector thresholds to avoid INT8-emulation for batch_size<=2 unless we see clear perf benefit; add a canary that biases toward fp16 for small-batch traffic.
Priya: I'll add an ops playbook entry: how to pin variants, rollback steps, and dashboard checks for KV-hit regressions.
Mateo: Also will investigate calibration pipeline: looks like per-channel scaling step mutated token prefix padding metadata in a way that affected KV keys. Need a test to ensure tokenization invariant after calib.
Noor: We need comms + follow-up timeline for ACME and a postmortem distribution list. Jules please include them.
Alex: We'll keep endpoint pinned until we validate a selector patch and deploy a proper fix. ETA for selector change + staging AB: 48-72 hours.
Jules: Will add ACME to postmortem distro and follow up once we have the selector patch and a rollback-proof canary. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
(THREAD CLOSED)
__notes: This thread captures a customer escalation about a quantization calibration rollout that caused the runtime to pick an INT8-emulation kernel, degrading latency and KV-cache behavior; includes repro, profiler excerpts, mitigation (pin to FP16), and action items.
